application.name: Shopping Sample App
application.description: Sample application demonstrating Flight Plan features

rolling.description: Gradually replace instances with the new version (no big-bang cutover).

canary.description: Shift a small percentage of traffic to the new version, then expand if healthy.

blueGreen.description: Deploy new version alongside old, then switch traffic over (fast rollback by switching back).

blue-green.description: Deploy new version alongside old, then switch traffic over (fast rollback by switching back).

ring.description: Progressively roll out by cohorts (rings) such as internal → beta → general.

recreate.description: Stop the old version and then start the new version (often implies downtime).

rollback.description: Revert to the previous version if health checks fail (switch back / redeploy previous).

roll-forward.description: Fix forward by deploying a new version rather than reverting (preferred when rollback is risky).

abort-canary.description: Stop a canary rollout and route traffic back to the stable version.

switchback.description: For blue/green, switch traffic back to the old environment quickly.

expand-contract.description: Two-phase schema change: add backwards-compatible changes, deploy app, then remove old fields.

backward-compatible.description: Migrations that can run without coordinated downtime and support old/new app versions.

big-bang.description: One coordinated cutover where app and schema change together (higher risk, often downtime).

dual-write.description: Write to both old and new stores during transition; eventually read from the new store.

shadow-read.description: Read from the new store in parallel (not serving) to validate behavior before cutover.

monolith.description: Single deployable unit containing most of the system.

modular-monolith.description: Single deployable with strong internal module boundaries.

microservices.description: Multiple independently deployable services communicating over the network.

event-driven.description: Asynchronous integration via events/streams; services react to published events.

serverless.description: Functions or managed runtimes with automatic scaling and per-execution billing.

batch.description: Scheduled or triggered jobs processing data in discrete runs.

api-gateway.description: Central entry point for routing, auth, rate limiting, and request shaping.

ingress-controller.description: Cluster ingress (e.g., Kubernetes Ingress) providing HTTP routing to services.

load-balancer.description: Layer 4/7 load balancer as the primary entry point.

service-mesh.description: Traffic enters via mesh gateway; mesh provides mTLS and routing between services.

direct.description: Clients connect directly to the service endpoint (generally avoid for external traffic).

edge.description: TLS terminates at the edge (gateway/load balancer); internal hops may be plaintext.

reencrypt.description: TLS terminates at the edge and traffic is re-encrypted to upstream services.

passthrough.description: TLS is not terminated at the edge; it passes through to the service.

end-to-end.description: TLS from client all the way to the service; intermediate hops preserve encryption.

mtls.description: Mutual TLS between hops (service-to-service identity and encryption).

https.description: HTTP over TLS (standard for web APIs and browsers).

http.description: HTTP without TLS (typically internal only; prefer https).

grpc.description: gRPC over HTTP/2 (often with TLS); strongly typed RPC.

websocket.description: Full-duplex messaging over a single TCP connection (ws/wss).

tcp.description: Raw TCP protocol (custom or non-HTTP services).

internal.description: Intended only for internal callers within the organization/system boundary.

external.description: Callable by external consumers; treat as a primary ingress surface.

public.description: Accessible publicly (no network restriction). Ensure strong authz and rate limiting.

partner.description: Accessible to specific partner networks/tenants; typically contract-bound.

none.description: No authentication (generally only for internal/private endpoints).

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 (often with OIDC) for delegated authorization via access tokens.

bearer.description: Bearer token (JWT or opaque); verify signature/issuer/audience/expiry.

api-key.description: Static token sent with requests; rotate regularly and scope permissions tightly.

mtls.description: Mutual TLS client certificates (strong transport-level client identity).

basic.description: HTTP Basic auth (avoid for external; only with TLS and strong password policies).

public-cloud.description: Runs primarily on a public cloud provider (AWS/Azure/GCP).

private-cloud.description: Runs on a private cloud or hosted private infrastructure.

on-prem.description: Runs in on-premises datacenters owned/operated by the organization.

hybrid.description: Runs across multiple environments (e.g., on-prem + cloud).

edge.description: Runs close to users/devices (edge sites), often latency-sensitive.

SaaS.description: Software-as-a-Service (multi-tenant or single-tenant product delivered to customers).

internal.description: Internal product/system used within the organization.

platform.description: Internal platform capability consumed by other teams (paved road).

managed-service.description: Service operated by a provider with defined SLOs and operational responsibilities.

single-tenant.description: Each customer has isolated resources (strong isolation, higher cost).

multi-tenant.description: Multiple customers share resources with logical isolation (efficiency, requires strong controls).

hybrid.description: Mix of single-tenant and multi-tenant patterns (e.g., shared control plane + isolated data plane).

database.description: Relational or document database used for durable storage.

topic.description: Publish/subscribe channel for messages or events.

object-storage.description: Blob/object storage for files and large unstructured data.

search.description: Search index (e.g., Elasticsearch/OpenSearch) for query and aggregation.

secrets.description: Secrets manager or key vault for credentials, API keys, and certificates.

service-to-service.description: A service calls another service (sync or async) via an interface/export.

service-to-resource.description: A service uses a resource (database, queue, storage, external system).

read.description: Reads data but does not modify it.

expected.description: A documented exception/expected crossing that should still be reviewed periodically.

exception.description: An explicit exception to normal policy (requires justification and review cadence).

low.description: Untrusted or internet-exposed zone; assume hostile traffic.

medium.description: Partially trusted zone (e.g., partner networks); apply strong boundary controls.

high.description: Highly trusted internal zone with strict access control.

on-call.description: A dedicated on-call rotation supports incidents and pages 24/7 or during business hours.

follow-the-sun.description: Support coverage handed off across time zones to provide continuous coverage.

best-effort.description: No formal incident response; support during business hours as available.

managed.description: A managed service/provider handles operations and incident response.

tier-0.description: Mission-critical; severe business impact if down (highest availability expectations).

tier-1.description: Critical; significant impact if down; strong SLOs and response expectations.

tier-2.description: Important; moderate impact; availability targets appropriate to business needs.

freeze.description: Pause feature work when error budget is exhausted; focus on reliability.

slow-down.description: Reduce change rate and increase guardrails when error budget is low.

none.description: No formal policy; track reliability but no explicit engineering trade-off.

snapshots.description: Periodic full snapshots/backups of data (restore point recovery).

continuous.description: Continuous backup or point-in-time recovery where available.

replicated.description: Data replicated to secondary region/site for durability and DR.

annually.description: Restore procedures are tested annually (generally too infrequent for critical systems).

none.description: No retries; failures surface immediately (may be appropriate for non-idempotent writes).

bounded.description: Limited retries with backoff and jitter; avoid thundering herds.

exponential-backoff.description: Retries with increasing delays; include jitter; cap maximum delay.

default.description: Reasonable timeouts enforced; avoid unbounded waits and resource exhaustion.

aggressive.description: Short timeouts for latency-sensitive paths; requires careful tuning.

required.description: Operations must be safe to retry (same request can be applied multiple times).

best-effort.description: Some operations are idempotent; document exceptions.

structured.description: Machine-parseable logs (JSON) with consistent fields and correlation IDs.

unstructured.description: Plaintext logs; harder to query and correlate.

golden-signals.description: Track latency, traffic, errors, and saturation (SRE golden signals).

business.description: Track product/business KPIs in addition to technical metrics.

none.description: No distributed tracing (rely on logs/metrics only).

per-client.description: Limit requests per consumer/client to protect service and enforce fairness.

global.description: Limit total traffic to protect downstream systems.

token-bucket.description: Token-bucket/leaky-bucket style limiting for smoothing bursts.

date-based.description: Version by date (e.g., 2026-01-01) often paired with deprecation windows.

timeboxed.description: Old versions are supported for a fixed time window with clear dates.

n-versions.description: Support the latest N versions; deprecate older versions.

shared.description: Tenants share compute/storage with logical isolation.

pooled.description: Resources are pooled but strongly partitioned per tenant.

siloed.description: Each tenant has dedicated resources (strongest isolation).

by-tenant-id.description: Partition data by tenant identifier (common for multi-tenant systems).

by-region.description: Partition data by geography/region; may also include tenant.

enforced.description: Authorization checks consistently enforce tenant boundaries at every layer.

partial.description: Some tenant checks exist; document gaps and remediation plan.

quotas.description: Per-tenant quotas/limits to prevent a single tenant from consuming all resources.

rate-limits.description: Per-tenant rate limits to smooth load and protect shared infrastructure.

isolation.description: Isolation via dedicated capacity or scheduling to reduce contention.

centralized.description: Authentication handled by a central identity provider/gateway; services trust propagated identity.

mfa.description: Multi-factor authentication is required for user sign-in (e.g., TOTP, WebAuthn/passkeys). Usually enforced by the IdP.

saml.description: SAML-based SSO (typically browser-facing apps) where an IdP issues assertions consumed by the application.

jwt.description: JWT-based auth where clients present signed tokens (bearer tokens) validated by the gateway and/or services (issuer/audience/expiry).

oidc.description: OpenID Connect (OIDC) sign-in and token issuance via an IdP (commonly paired with OAuth2 access tokens).

session-cookie.description: Server-managed session using secure cookies (often for browser apps); requires CSRF protections and secure session storage.

required.description: Security-relevant actions are logged with actor, action, target, and outcome.

best-effort.description: Some audit logging exists; document gaps and improve over time.

enabled.description: Stored data is encrypted at rest using managed keys or KMS.

tls.description: TLS used for network transport encryption.

mtls.description: Mutual TLS used between services for both encryption and identity.

vault.description: Secrets stored in a dedicated secrets manager (vault/key vault) with rotation.

env-vars.description: Secrets injected via environment variables (acceptable with strong runtime controls).

kms.description: Keys managed via a KMS/HSM-backed service.

hsm.description: Hardware security module (highest assurance) for key storage and operations.

this-system.description: This system is the authoritative source for this data domain.

external.description: An external system is authoritative; this system caches/replicates/derives data.

indefinite.description: Data retained without a defined expiration (avoid unless required).

timeboxed.description: Data retained for a fixed period (e.g., 30/90/365 days) then deleted/archived.

hard-delete.description: Data is permanently removed (required for some compliance cases).

soft-delete.description: Data is marked deleted but retained for recovery/forensics until purged.

least-privilege.description: Access is granted minimally; default deny; periodic review and rotation.

broad.description: Broad access (avoid); document compensating controls and review cadence.

hipaa.description: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (US healthcare).

pci-dss.description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard.
